newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK economic pick-up seen sustained thru 1997 - Tsang.
newsitem.headline: HK economic pick-up seen sustained thru 1997 - Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Thursday that Hong Kong's economy was picking up, with economic growth in the fourth quarter even better than in the third.

"I believe that our economic growth is picking up along the established locus of five percent increase a year and that this performance will sustain through 1997," Tsang said in a speech to the Chinese Manufacturers Association.

Tsang said a steady revival in consumer spending, moderate growth in exports and investment, and an improved trade balance had brought the gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate above the trend level in the third quarter.
"We reckon growth in the fourth quarter to be even better," he said.

The government in November estimated third quarter GDP growth at 5.0 to 5.5 percent year on year, against 3.3 and 4.3 percent in the first and second quarters respectively. It also maintained its 1996 full-year growth forecast at 4.7 percent.
Tsang also noted that 1996 inflation was forecast at a 6.0 percent, lower than previous expectations, and that the overall resource situation was less stringent than before.
"In short, we have both the momentum and the capacity to improve on our performance in the short and medium terms," he said.
External demand would not be lacking with export growth to major markets expected to be at least sustained, and China was also bouncing back from its successful soft landing, he said.
Tsang said that in tackling current economic issues, Hong Kong would not depart from its basic non-interventionist stance.
He reiterated the importance of the rule of law, a level-playing field, a lean and corruption-free civil service and a free flow of information for Hong Kong's continued economic advance.
